passages.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I feel so far from home, like I don’t belong anywhere anymore.  
I wonder if God still remembers us out here, scattered and alone.  
It’s hard to keep my faith strong when I’m surrounded by people who don’t understand our ways.  
I miss the old days, when we were all together—now I just feel lost.  
I struggle to serve God faithfully when every day brings new challenges in this foreign land.  
I worry that being so far from our people means I’ll forget who I am.  
It’s difficult to greet each day with hope when everything familiar has been taken from me.  
I feel like an outsider, and sometimes I question if I’ll ever find true community again.  
I want to be a good servant, but I’m not sure how to do that when I’m so isolated.  
I keep asking myself if there’s a purpose to all this wandering and separation.
passages.original: Ἰάκωβος Θεοῦ καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος Ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ Διασπορᾷ Χαίρειν

passages.text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.
passages.struggle:
I keep facing one hardship after another, and I just can’t see how I’m supposed to be joyful about it.  
Every time something goes wrong, I wonder if I’m being punished instead of tested.  
It’s hard for me to believe that anything good can come from all these troubles I’m going through.  
I feel worn out by all these challenges, and I don’t know how to keep going with a positive attitude.  
When life gets tough, I start doubting if my faith is strong enough to handle it.  
I hear people talk about finding joy in hard times, but honestly, I just feel frustrated and tired.  
Sometimes I wonder if I’ll ever have the patience to get through these trials without giving up.  
I struggle to see the purpose behind my suffering, and it makes me question if I’m growing at all.  
Everyone says to stay strong, but I feel like I’m barely holding on most days.  
I want to believe that these tests will make me better, but right now, it just feels overwhelming.
passages.original: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε ἀδελφοί μου ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν

passages.text: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
passages.struggle:
I keep giving up halfway through my troubles, and I wonder if I’ll ever really grow stronger.  
Sometimes I get so impatient for things to get better that I don’t let myself learn what I’m supposed to.  
I feel like I’m always missing something important in my life, no matter how hard I try.  
It’s hard for me to believe that sticking it out through hard times will actually make me whole.  
I worry that I’ll never be the kind of person who’s truly complete or mature.  
When things get tough, I just want to escape instead of letting the struggle change me.  
I see others who seem so put together, and I wonder why I still feel so unfinished.  
I’m afraid that if I keep waiting and enduring, I’ll just end up empty-handed.  
Sometimes I question if perseverance really leads to anything good, or if I’m just fooling myself.  
I struggle to trust that there’s a purpose in letting patience do its work in me.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι

passages.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
passages.struggle:
I keep making the same mistakes and wonder if I’ll ever learn what’s right.  
Sometimes I feel lost and wish I knew what to do next, but I’m afraid to ask for help.  
I worry that I’m not smart enough to understand what’s happening around me.  
I want to make good choices, but I don’t know where to turn for guidance.  
I feel embarrassed to admit that I don’t have all the answers.  
It’s hard for me to believe that someone would help me without judging me.  
I’m not sure if I deserve to be given wisdom when I’ve failed so many times.  
I hear people talk about seeking guidance, but I don’t know how to start.  
I’m afraid that if I ask for help, I’ll just be a burden to others.  
Sometimes I wonder if anyone really listens when I pray for understanding.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος Θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ

passages.text: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I pray, but deep down I’m not sure if anyone’s really listening.  
I keep changing my mind about what I believe, and it leaves me feeling lost.  
When trouble comes, I start to question if I can really trust that things will work out.  
I want to ask for help, but I’m afraid my doubts will get in the way.  
One day I feel strong in my faith, and the next I’m full of uncertainty.  
I worry that my prayers won’t be answered because I can’t stop second-guessing myself.  
It feels like my heart is being pulled in two directions, and I can’t find steady ground.  
I wish I could just believe without all these questions swirling in my mind.  
Every time I try to trust, fear creeps in and shakes me like a stormy sea.  
I’m tired of feeling unstable, like I’m drifting wherever the wind blows.
passages.original: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει μηδὲν διακρινόμενος ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ

passages.text: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
passages.struggle:
I keep asking for help, but deep down I don’t really believe anything will change for me.  
Sometimes I wonder if my prayers even matter, or if I’m just talking to the wind.  
I want to trust, but I always have this nagging doubt that God won’t answer me.  
It feels like I’m just going through the motions, not really expecting anything good to come.  
I see others receiving blessings, but I can’t shake the feeling that nothing is meant for me.  
Every time I ask for guidance, I second-guess whether I’m worthy to receive it.  
I struggle to believe that God would actually listen to someone like me.  
When I pray, I can’t help but think I’m wasting my breath.  
I feel like my doubts are keeping me from ever getting what I truly need.  
No matter how much I ask, I just can’t expect anything to happen.
passages.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
passages.struggle:
Some days I feel pulled in two directions, and I can’t seem to make up my mind about anything.  
I keep changing my plans because I’m never sure what I really want.  
I say I trust, but then I second-guess every decision I make.  
I feel like I’m always wavering, never steady on my feet.  
No matter what I choose, I’m haunted by doubts that I made the wrong call.  
I want to be firm in my beliefs, but I keep hesitating and it leaves me restless.  
It’s like I’m always caught between two opinions, and it’s exhausting.  
I wish I could just stick to one path instead of jumping from one thing to another.  
My heart feels divided, and it’s making it hard to move forward.  
I’m tired of feeling so unsettled in everything I do.
passages.original: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.
passages.struggle:
I don’t understand how I’m supposed to feel proud when I have so little compared to everyone else.
Sometimes I wonder if my low status means I’m less important in God’s eyes.
It’s hard to see any reason to celebrate my situation when I’m always struggling to get by.
I feel invisible most days, like no one notices me or what I do.
People look down on me because I don’t have much, and it makes me question my worth.
I keep hearing that I should rejoice, but I just feel ashamed of where I am in life.
When others talk about their successes, I feel left out and forgotten.
I want to believe there’s honor in my humble life, but it’s hard when the world says otherwise.
Sometimes I doubt that my circumstances could ever be something to be glad about.
I struggle to see how my low position could ever be considered a blessing.
passages.original: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
passages.struggle:
I keep worrying that all my wealth will disappear overnight, and then what will I have left?  
Sometimes I wonder if people only respect me because of my riches, not for who I really am.  
It’s hard for me to feel humble when everyone treats me like I’m important just because of my money.  
I fear that everything I’ve built will fade away, and I’ll be forgotten like yesterday’s news.  
When I look at my possessions, I can’t help but feel how temporary it all is.  
I struggle to find meaning beyond my success, especially when I realize how quickly fortunes can change.  
There are days when I feel empty, even though I have more than enough.  
I wish I knew how to be content with less, but I’m afraid of losing my status.  
Sometimes I envy those who seem happy with little, while I’m always chasing after more.  
It’s difficult to accept that my wealth won’t last, no matter how hard I try to hold onto it.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται

passages.text: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
passages.struggle:
I used to take pride in all I owned, but lately it feels like everything I’ve built is slipping through my fingers.  
Sometimes I wonder if all my hard work and success really matter, when it can all disappear so quickly.  
I look in the mirror and barely recognize myself—my youth and strength are fading, and I can’t stop it.  
No matter how much I chase after, it never seems to last; it’s like watching a beautiful flower wilt in the sun.  
I see others admiring my wealth, but inside I feel empty, as if all this will vanish before I know it.  
Lately, I fear that my achievements are just temporary, and I worry what will be left when they’re gone.  
I’ve spent my life pursuing more, but now I’m afraid I’ll be forgotten just as quickly as a flower withers.  
It troubles me how quickly beauty and fortune can fade, leaving nothing behind but memories.  
Even in the midst of my busy life, I can’t shake the feeling that everything I value is fragile and fleeting.
passages.original: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται

passages.text: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.
passages.struggle:
I keep wondering if all these hardships are worth it in the end.  
Sometimes I feel like giving up when things get tough, but I want to believe there's a reward for holding on.  
It's hard to stay faithful when it feels like my troubles never end.  
I see others give in to temptation so easily, and I question if I have the strength to resist.  
I worry that my love for God isn't enough to get me through these trials.  
When I'm tested, I feel alone and unsure if anyone notices my struggle.  
I hear about a crown of life, but I can't help but doubt if it's really meant for someone like me.  
Every time I face a new challenge, I wonder if I'm being punished or if there's a purpose behind it.  
I want to persevere, but sometimes the weight of my burdens makes me want to quit.  
I struggle to trust that there's a promise waiting for me on the other side of all this pain.
passages.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I wonder if these hardships are some kind of test from above, and it makes me feel lost.  
I keep blaming God whenever I stumble, but deep down I know it’s not really His doing.  
It’s hard not to think that my struggles are punishments sent to me, even though I know that’s not right.  
When I’m tempted, I catch myself asking why God would let this happen, and I feel guilty for thinking that way.  
I get angry and say things like, “Why is God making this so hard for me?” even though I know He isn’t the one tempting me.  
I struggle to accept that my own choices lead me into trouble, not some plan from above.  
Sometimes I feel like giving up and blaming someone else, but I know I need to take responsibility for my actions.  
It’s confusing when bad things happen, and I want to believe there’s a reason, but I’m not sure what to think.  
I wish I could stop thinking that every challenge is a trap set for me, instead of just life happening.
passages.original: Μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πειράζομαι ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα

passages.text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.
passages.struggle:
I keep finding myself wanting things I know aren’t good for me, and it’s hard to say no.  
Sometimes I wonder why I always seem to chase after what I shouldn’t, even when I know better.  
It feels like my own heart is pulling me in the wrong direction, and I don’t know how to fight it.  
I blame others for my mistakes, but deep down I know it’s my own desires leading me astray.  
No matter how much I try, I can’t seem to stop wanting what I know is wrong.  
I get so easily distracted by things that promise happiness, but they always leave me empty.  
I wish I could control my cravings, but they seem to control me instead.  
It’s hard to admit, but sometimes I choose what I want over what’s right.  
I feel trapped by my own longings, like I’m being pulled along by something inside me.  
Even when I try to do good, my own desires keep getting in the way.
passages.original: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος

passages.text: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
passages.struggle:
I keep telling myself it’s just a small craving, but every time I give in, it feels like I’m slipping further away from who I want to be.
  
Sometimes I wonder how something that starts as a harmless thought can end up causing so much trouble in my life.

I feel trapped, like my own desires are leading me down a path I know I shouldn’t follow.

It scares me how easy it is for a little temptation to grow into something that hurts me and those around me.

I wish I could stop before things get out of hand, but once I start, it’s like I can’t turn back.

I never meant for my choices to bring so much pain, but now I see the consequences piling up.

There are days when I feel like I’m fighting a losing battle against my own wants.

I keep hoping I can control myself, but it always seems to spiral into something worse than I expected.

I’m afraid that if I don’t change, I’ll end up losing everything that matters to me.
passages.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον

passages.text: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I worry that I'm believing something just because it sounds good, not because it's true.  
I keep getting confused by all the different voices telling me what’s right and wrong.  
I thought I was on the right path, but now I’m not so sure anymore.  
It’s hard to know who to trust when everyone claims to have the answers.  
I feel like I’ve been led astray before, and I’m afraid it could happen again.  
There are days when I doubt if I really understand what’s good and what’s not.  
I want to follow what’s true, but sometimes my own desires get in the way.  
I’m scared of being tricked by things that look good on the outside but aren’t.  
I struggle to tell the difference between what I want to hear and what I need to hear.  
I wish it was easier to see through the lies and hold on to what’s real.
passages.original: Μὴ πλανᾶσθε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί

passages.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I wonder if the good things in my life are really blessings, or if I just got lucky.  
I keep worrying that what I have will be taken away, like maybe it’s all too good to last.  
It’s hard for me to trust that anything truly good can come from someone I can’t see.  
I struggle to believe that someone out there cares enough to give me anything perfect.  
When things go wrong, I start to doubt if there’s anyone steady or dependable looking out for me.  
I often compare what I have to others and feel like I’m missing out on the best gifts.  
I get confused about what’s really good for me and what just looks good on the outside.  
Sometimes I feel like I have to earn every good thing, instead of just receiving it.  
I worry that if I mess up, the good things in my life will disappear.  
It’s hard for me to accept that someone could give without changing their mind or holding it over me.
passages.original: πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς τῶν φώτων παρ’ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα

passages.text: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.
passages.struggle:
Sometimes I wonder if I really have a purpose, or if I’m just another face in the crowd.  
I struggle to believe that I could be special to God when I feel so ordinary.  
It’s hard for me to accept that I was chosen for something good when my past is so full of mistakes.  
I keep asking myself what it means to be set apart, because I don’t feel any different from anyone else.  
There are days when I doubt that the truth I’ve heard can actually change who I am inside.  
I feel pressure to live up to being an example, but I’m afraid I’ll let everyone down.  
Sometimes I question if I really belong among those who are called to something greater.  
I worry that I’m not living up to what I was meant to be, even though I want to.  
It’s difficult for me to see myself as a new creation when old habits keep coming back.  
I often feel unworthy of being called a firstfruit, like I’m not good enough for that honor.
passages.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων

passages.text: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.
passages.struggle:
I keep snapping at people before I even hear what they're trying to say.  
Sometimes I speak without thinking, and it always seems to make things worse.  
I get angry so quickly, and afterward I regret the things I said.  
It's hard for me to listen patiently when I feel like I'm being wronged.  
I want to do what's right, but my temper always gets the better of me.  
I struggle to hold my tongue when I feel frustrated or misunderstood.  
Even when I try to stay calm, I find myself raising my voice before I realize it.  
I wish I could be slower to anger, but it feels like my emotions take over.  
People tell me I don't really listen to them, and I think they're right.  
I know I should be more patient, but I just can't seem to control my reactions.
passages.original: Ἴστε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται

passages.text: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.
passages.struggle:
I keep falling back into old habits, even though I know they're not right.  
Sometimes I feel like there's too much darkness in me to really change.  
It's hard for me to let go of the anger and bitterness I've carried for so long.  
I struggle to accept what’s good for me, especially when pride gets in the way.  
There are days when I wonder if I can ever truly be free from the things that hold me back.  
I hear about living a better way, but I find it difficult to actually welcome it into my heart.  
Letting go of the things I know are wrong feels like losing a part of myself.  
I want to believe that something planted deep inside me can really save me, but doubt keeps creeping in.  
Even when I try to do better, I feel surrounded by so much evil in the world.  
I wish I could accept what’s true with a gentle spirit, but I always want to fight and resist.
passages.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν

passages.text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.
passages.struggle:
I hear all these teachings, but I never seem to put them into practice when it matters most.  
Sometimes I feel like I know what’s right, but I just don’t follow through.  
It’s easy for me to listen to good advice, but actually living it out is a whole different story.  
I worry that I’m just fooling myself by thinking I’m faithful when my actions don’t show it.  
I sit in the gatherings and nod along, but when I leave, I forget to act on what I’ve learned.  
I want to be more than just someone who listens—I want my life to show what I believe, but I keep falling short.  
There are days when I feel like I’m just going through the motions, not really living out what I say I believe.  
I struggle with the fear that I’m deceiving myself, thinking I’m doing enough just by hearing the word.  
I know the right things to do, but I keep putting them off, telling myself I’ll start tomorrow.  
It bothers me that I can talk about faith so easily, but my actions don’t always match my words.
passages.original: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς

passages.text: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror, and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.
passages.struggle:
I listen to all the teachings, but when I leave, I can’t seem to remember how I’m supposed to live them out.  
Every time I hear a good message, I feel inspired, but by the next day, I’ve already slipped back into my old habits.  
Sometimes I wonder if I really know myself at all, because I keep forgetting what I promised to change.  
I keep hearing what’s right, but when it comes time to act, I just forget and do nothing.  
It’s like I catch a glimpse of who I should be, but as soon as I turn away, it all fades from my mind.  
I want to be better, but I keep losing sight of what matters as soon as I leave the gathering.  
I feel like I’m always learning, but never actually living out what I’ve learned.  
No matter how many times I’m reminded, I walk away and forget what I’m supposed to do.  
I recognize my faults when I’m listening, but I can’t seem to hold onto that awareness once I’m on my own.  
It troubles me that I can see the truth for a moment, but then I just go back to my old ways as if nothing changed.
passages.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν

passages.text: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.
passages.struggle:
I keep reading about what’s right, but when it comes time to act, I just freeze up and forget everything I learned.
Sometimes I feel like I understand what’s good, but I struggle to actually live it out day after day.
I worry that I’m just going through the motions, hearing all these teachings but not really letting them change how I live.
It’s hard for me to stay focused on what’s true and not get distracted by everything else going on.
I want to do what’s right, but I get discouraged when I don’t see results right away.
I often wonder if I’m missing out on blessings because I don’t follow through with what I know I should do.
There are days when I feel inspired, but by the next morning, I’ve already forgotten my resolve.
I struggle to keep my commitment strong, especially when it feels easier to just listen and not act.
I’m afraid I’ll never be the kind of person who actually puts these words into practice.
It’s tough to keep looking for guidance and not give up when things get difficult.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται

passages.text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
passages.struggle:
I keep saying things I regret, even though I want to live a good life.  
Sometimes my words hurt people, and I wonder if my faith means anything at all.  
I talk about doing the right thing, but I can't seem to control my temper when I speak.  
I worry that my actions don't match what I claim to believe.  
It's hard for me to hold my tongue when I'm angry, and I feel like I'm letting myself and God down.  
I tell others how to live, but then I gossip without thinking.  
I want to be a good example, but my words often betray me.  
I feel like I'm fooling myself when I act religious but can't stop speaking harshly.  
No matter how much I pray, I still slip up and say things I shouldn't.  
I wonder if all my efforts are pointless when I can't control what comes out of my mouth.
passages.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία

passages.text: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.
passages.struggle:
I keep telling myself I care about others, but when I see someone in real need, I just walk on by.  
Sometimes I wonder if I’m really living the way I should, or if I’m just going through the motions.  
It’s hard for me to help people who are suffering when I feel like I have nothing left to give.  
I worry that the world’s ways are rubbing off on me more than I realize.  
I want to help those who are alone, but I’m afraid of getting too involved or making things worse.  
I see widows and orphans struggling, but I don’t know how to reach out without feeling awkward.  
I try to keep myself pure, but temptation is everywhere and I slip up more than I’d like to admit.  
Sometimes I feel like my faith is just words, not actions, and that bothers me.  
I get so caught up in my own problems that I forget about those who have it even harder.  
I’m not sure how to stay untainted by the world when I’m surrounded by so much pressure to fit in.
passages.original: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου
